newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-MCMANUS BATTLES BACK FROM BRINK OF DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-MCMANUS BATTLES BACK FROM BRINK OF DEFEAT.

text.p: World number six Alan McManus battled back from the brink of defeat to win his first round match in the world snooker championship on Tuesday.
McManus, 8-4 down at one stage to fellow Scot Billy Snaddon, was never ahead until he potted the opening red in the deciding 19th frame.
The decider was scrappy with McManus leading 43-0 and then being pegged back to 44-31 before he fluked the final brown to leave Snaddon needing snookers.
Snaddon, who has fallen at the first hurdle in three outings at the world championship, said he had thrown the match away.
McManus, a semifinalist at Sheffield in 1992 and 1993, said: "When I went 8-4 down I thought I was on the way out. I was feeling down but Billy started to make a few mistakes."
